text:
aisha: Heads up — on canary infra I'm seeing a slow memory siphon during very long streaming tool-loop sessions (12k+ tokens). Not a hard OOM, just steady growth ~30-40MB/hour on the kv cache worker. Repro steps below and a tiny flame snippet.

matt: rough numbers? which binary (runtime/cpu/gpu) and kernel picks?

aisha: runtime: inferenced-canary-2026-03-16, gcpu path on A100, model: longchat-13b-fp16, batching=continuous, batch size cap 64. Kernel selection: auto (fp16-optimized). Growth seen only when tool chains call out >100 short tool outputs per session.

jin: can you paste the flame snippet / jemalloc output?

aisha: pasted below — short.
```
flame: top hot: kv::page_walk (25%), kv::retain_slot (18%), allocator::arena_grow (9%), batcher::flush_if_stalled (6%)
jemalloc: small increase in inactive spans over time, leak counters show 'pinned_pages' rising slowly
perf sample: many stack traces from page_walk triggered by cache lookup misses for long prefix keys
```

devon: so it sounds like repeated prefix mismatches causing page_walk churn + arena growth. Could be fragmentation from repeated small allocations in tool result parsing. Have we ruled out application-level retention (user context pins)?

aisha: yes — I instrumented session metadata and KV references; reference counts drop when messages end. The growth is in internal page metadata and some slab tailing. Not full refs.

matt: try toggling kernel selection to fp32-optimized and disable continuous batching for a single run — if kernel affects memory layout of KV pages maybe allocator behavior changes. Also run jemalloc stats and jeprof.

aisha: ran quick toggles, results:
```
- fp32-kernel + batcher=per-request -> growth slows to ~5MB/hr
- fp16-kernel + continous batching -> growth as before ~35MB/hr
- A/B shows pattern consistent, so kernel + batching interplay matters
```

jin: interesting. Could be that continuous batching causes internal buffers to coalesce keys leading to different allocation lifetimes; kernel choice affects vector sizes/alignments so slab placement differs. We should gather: jemalloc stats over time (sn_malloc, sn_active), a heap profile (jeprof), and a short perf mmap trace.

aisha: collecting: jeprof heapdump at start, +1h, +4h. Also attached a small reproducer command:
```
# repro (internal)
python tools/long_stream_repro.py --model longchat-13b --tokens 12000 --toolchain rapid-echo --batch=continuous --kernel=fp16 --clients=3
```

devon: can ops-bot run that on canary for 6 hours with jemalloc logging enabled? tag me if you see >200MB delta.

ops-bot: @devon scheduled job r-3812 on canary-cluster-5. Logs are streaming to /canary/logs/r-3812. Will report jeprof dumps at 1h/4h/6h.

matt: another angle — we've seen allocator fragmentation when small objects are allocated in a long-lived arena mixed with ephemeral ones. If batcher holds onto ephemeral buffers until flush, that could pin pages. Can you try a patch that moves ephemeral parse buffers to a separate arena (opt-in) and run for 2h?

aisha: I'll try the arena split patch on a dev node first. Quick grep shows parsers allocate ~256-2k objects per tool output. Splitting could keep ephemeral objects in a short-lived arena and reduce tail fragmentation.

jin: also add a periodic compact/hint call in the kv page sweeper (no more than once per 30m) to reclaim empty spans. We avoided that earlier for latency but a low-frequency hint might help long sessions.

aisha: agreed — I'll test both independently: arena-split + batcher change vs periodic compact. Will post results in this thread.

matt: thanks — if either mitigates, we can plan a canary rollout. If neither do, next step is to instrument page_walk to log key patterns and produce minimal reproducer keys to feed into a unit test.

devon: noted. Also add a perf map sample during the run to capture kernel selection impacts.

aisha: initial dev-run results: arena-split reduces growth to ~8MB/hr; periodic compact reduces it to ~10MB/hr. Combining both on canary now. ops-bot will report.

ops-bot: canary run r-3812 combined-patch finished 6h: observed peak delta 48MB vs baseline 210MB. Jeprof attached to logs.

aisha: great — looks like fragmentation + batching interaction. Action items:
- matt: review arena-split patch, add config flag and telemetry (who uses ephemeral arena)
- jin: add low-frequency compact hint and a metric for compacted_spans_count
- devex: add test harness for long-tool-loop allocations (repro script)
- ops: schedule canary rollout with combined fix for next week

matt: will do PR today. Also add a benchmarking run to ensure latency SLOs unaffected.

jin: I'll add compact telemetry + a lightweight unit test that simulates repeated short tool outputs with continuous batching.

aisha: thanks team. I'll mark this as triaged and close after two successful canary runs.
